findings.text: _launched_candidates decides which pointers a search may answer with by reading the queued phase alone, and ignores launched_at, while the repository already owns that decision at reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py:175 (awaits_a_lane_slot), whose docstring says a pointer carrying launched_at is launched whatever its phase says; the new named definition duplicates the owner's predicate rather than extending it, so a review that launched before its phase write is excluded from the search and the duty reads missing - the same coarser rule the two inline citations it replaces already used, now fixed under a name that reads as authoritative.

_standing_review's docstring still says a pointer handed in from outside the pass 'is answered by its own sweep', but c2c8909eb6 changed that fallback to _pointer_review, which makes one search over the launched candidates and no sweep at all; the paragraph now describes a cost the code does not pay, and a reader budgeting this path from the docstring will overstate it by the size of the live set.

the repair edits reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py, which neither the plan section's write paths (reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_a_duty_pass_reads_reviews_in_flight_once.py and the node's fragment) nor the dispatch node's declared paths cover; the manifest discloses it as a scope note in evidence_inputs under the shared-file ruling, so it needs the coordinator's ratification rather than a repair, but it is out of the fence as delivered.

the closing assertion 'head == base is None' compares _refused_delivered_review's answer with the same function's answer after monkeypatching _standing_review; if that function stopped consulting _standing_review the monkeypatch would change nothing and both sides would move together, so the assertion cannot redden on that regression and guards the reader's own answer rather than the function's use of it.

_standing returns None whenever _standing_review is absent from the module, so the queued case's 'in (None, "")' assertion passes unchanged if the reader is renamed or removed; the only thing that catches the removal is the sibling _current_review_in_flight call raising AttributeError, so the line reads as a guard it is not.
